But it also contains a lot of persistence logic, which belongs to the infrastructure layer. It calls the Prisma ORM client directly (`prismaService.order.findMany/create/update/delete/deleteMany/count/aggregate/findUnique`). It also builds complex, database-specific queries: in getActivities it assembles `Prisma.OrderWhereInput` filters, including case-insensitive `startsWith` matching, null checks on `SymbolProfileOverrides`, and the `orderBy` list. It reshapes ORM write inputs by mutating `connectOrCreate` and `connect` and deleting fields before writing. The private `orders()` method is a plain repository-style wrapper around `findMany`. None of this goes through a repository or other infrastructure abstraction, so the file carries infrastructure (persistence) responsibilities that the layer model assigns elsewhere, for example to `*.repository.ts`.
